chapter: Depression years and New Orleans trumpeters
title: Spot work, then going broke in 1929
summary: His sidemen played with him for spot work; steady engagements came only with the Depression. He lost his money in 1929 managing Atlanta's Con Corporation, then went back to New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Did he play in your band? Did you play with him?

Oh, he's played with me. All those boys played with me years ago. You see, we did mostly spot work. We never played steady engagements until the Depression hitters. I went broke in 29. I was managing the Con Atlanta Corporation, Atlanta, Georgia, on North Broad Street. And of course, then I went back to New Orleans. I had a home out in Avondale Estates and had one in New Orleans. Trying to keep them up. I didn't jump out of any window, however. I just lost it. Do you smoke?
I'll be glad for you to have one.
Oh, we better not mention brands on here.
